findings.excerpt: title: "Representations of the quiver 1 -> 2 in abelian groups form an abelian category"
findings.symptom: The rendered title visibly prints the ASCII arrow markup “1 -> 2”; the item body correctly renders the quiver as $1\to2$.

diagram_candidates.certainty: editorial candidate; mathematically explicit, but text currently states the square accurately
diagram_candidates.excerpt: A representation is $u:A_1\to A_2$, and a morphism of such representations is a commutative square.
diagram_candidates.maps_and_check: Show $A_1\xrightarrow{u}A_2$, $B_1\xrightarrow{v}B_2$, and vertical homomorphisms $f_1:A_1\to B_1$, $f_2:A_2\to B_2$; check $f_2u=vf_1$.
diagram_candidates.reason: The square is the concrete morphism data singled out by the example, but the current explanation is already concise.

diagram_candidates.certainty: editorial candidate; algebraic check is complete without a figure
diagram_candidates.excerpt: The two canonical endomorphisms are represented by $\sigma_1\sigma_2$ and $\sigma_2\sigma_1$.
diagram_candidates.maps_and_check: Draw both three-strand braid words using the library crossing convention; check that their endpoint permutations are $(1\,2\,3)$ and $(1\,3\,2)$, respectively, hence distinct.
diagram_candidates.reason: A paired braid figure would make the distinction tangible, while the existing permutation argument already proves it.

diagram_candidates.reason: This square is the result itself; a compact square could clarify what the arrow-category argument establishes.
